feed.title: Data Science & ML — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Academic Torrents
entry.summary: A community archive distributing large research datasets over BitTorrent. Against institutional download links the difference is durability: when the university server goes away, the data survives in the swarm.

entry.title: An Introduction to Statistical Learning
entry.summary: The standard introduction to statistical learning, free as a PDF with separate R and Python labs. Against "Elements of Statistical Learning" by the same authors it trades mathematics for intuition — this is the one you read first.

entry.title: Dataset List
entry.summary: A directory of machine learning datasets by domain, with size, licence and paper links. Against Kaggle these are academic and industrial sets rather than competition data — for when you need something real.

entry.title: ImageNet
entry.summary: A dataset of fourteen million images labelled against the WordNet hierarchy. What sets it apart from other image sets is historical weight: the 2012 deep learning breakthrough came out of the competition on it, and it is still a benchmark.

entry.title: Kaggle
entry.summary: Competitions, datasets and notebooks on one platform. The real value is that winning solutions are published once a contest closes, making it the best open archive of applied ML.

entry.title: AIMA
entry.summary: The companion site for Artificial Intelligence: A Modern Approach, publishing course code and algorithm implementations in several languages.

entry.title: DeepLearning.AI
entry.summary: Andrew Ng’s education platform, offering structured specialisations in deep learning and generative AI.

entry.title: fast.ai
entry.summary: Teaches deep learning top-down — a working model first, theory after. The exact inverse of the academic courses that open with mathematics.

entry.title: Keras
entry.summary: A high-level API reducing network construction to stacking layers in a few lines. It now runs on TensorFlow, PyTorch and JAX alike, which lets you defer the framework choice.

entry.title: Machine Learning Mastery
entry.summary: Application-focused ML tutorials, each ending in working code — answering “how do I do this” rather than the theory.

entry.title: Matplotlib
entry.summary: The foundation of Python plotting — seaborn and pandas’ plotting are built on it. It gives fine control at the cost of considerable code even for a simple chart.

entry.title: ML Crash Course
entry.summary: Google’s fast introduction to machine learning, moving through short video, reading and runnable exercises.

entry.title: mlcourse.ai
entry.summary: An open machine learning course whose pairing of theory with Kaggle competition assignments separates it from lecture-only material.

entry.title: MLU-Explain
entry.summary: Amazon’s set explaining machine learning concepts through interactive visuals — you drag a parameter and watch the model change.

entry.title: pandas
entry.summary: The standard library for tabular data. Unlike Excel every transformation is reproducible code; it works in memory, so the data has to fit in RAM.

entry.title: Plotly
entry.summary: An interactive charting library with zoom, tooltips and selection built in. Matplotlib produces a static image; this produces a chart you can explore in the browser.

entry.title: Polars
entry.summary: A DataFrame library written in Rust. Unlike pandas it uses every core and optimises the query before running it through lazy evaluation, which makes it multiples faster on large files.

entry.title: Power BI
entry.summary: Microsoft’s business intelligence tool with native connections to Excel and Azure sources. If the organisation is already on Microsoft 365, its real edge over Tableau is a licence that is already paid for.

entry.title: PySpark
entry.summary: Apache Spark’s Python interface, for when the data no longer fits on one machine. It offers a pandas-like API while distributing the work across a cluster.

entry.title: scikit-learn
entry.summary: The standard Python library for classical machine learning — classification, regression, clustering and preprocessing behind one `fit`/`predict` interface. The common ground for everything before deep learning.

entry.title: seaborn
entry.summary: A statistical plotting library on top of Matplotlib, reducing distribution, relationship and category plots to one line — with sane defaults out of the box.

entry.title: SerpentAI
entry.summary: A framework turning any video game into a reinforcement learning environment — working against real games rather than simulations is what makes it unusual.

entry.title: Streamlit
entry.summary: Turns a Python script into a web app in a few lines with no HTML, CSS or JavaScript — the shortest path for a data scientist to show a model to a stakeholder.

entry.title: Tableau
entry.summary: A drag-and-drop business intelligence platform for building dashboards without code. Common in enterprise reporting and weak on reproducibility and version control.

entry.title: TensorFlow
entry.summary: Google’s deep learning framework. It lost research ground to PyTorch, yet remains strong for mobile and embedded deployment (TF Lite) and production serving (TF Serving).

entry.title: Train LLM from Scratch
entry.summary: Shows the whole pipeline in working code, from data download to distributed training — the infrastructure side theoretical write-ups usually skip.

entry.title: Databricks
entry.summary: A data and ML platform built on Spark, bringing ACID guarantees to the data lake through Delta Lake — which is the technical substance behind the “lakehouse” claim.

entry.title: ARC Prize 2026
entry.summary: A competition on abstract reasoning whose tasks are designed to be easy for humans and hard for models. It rewards a new approach rather than more scale.

entry.title: LLMs from Scratch
entry.summary: A book repo that has you write a GPT from scratch in PyTorch — tokeniser, attention, training loop, fine-tuning. You build the mechanism instead of calling a library.

entry.title: Google Dataset Search
entry.summary: Searches open datasets scattered across the web via schema.org markup. Being tied to no single repository, it reaches institutional archives too.

entry.title: Zero to Mastery ML
entry.summary: End-to-end ML notebooks walking a working pipeline from data cleaning to model evaluation, progressing through real code rather than concept prose.

entry.title: Data Science for Beginners
entry.summary: A 20-lesson curriculum where each unit ships with pre/post quizzes and a project. Its data ethics and visualisation sections cover ground most technical courses skip.

entry.title: ML Mühendisliğinde İş Arama
entry.summary: An ML engineer’s account of a job hunt with the numbers — applications sent, stages reached, what worked. First-hand data against generic career advice.

entry.title: Kaggle Yarışmaları
entry.summary: Active and past competitions. Being scored against a real metric breaks the “looks fine to me” illusion of working on your own project.
